He took a rifle from one of the guards. He ordered Ramiz Milanovic to lie on the floor on his stomach. He cocked the rifle. He ordered him to lie down, and he put the rifle on the back of his head and said that he would count to ten. And he told the other guards to move away so that nothing would spray them. And indeed, the countdown started. Then somebody got in from the hallway, and said "Savo, there's somebody on the phone for you," so he went out. And this person who had said that said,"Listen, you guys, you are hiding this one Ekrem Zekovic, and can't you see that you're all going to get killed?" After that, we were ordered go to the other building where Room 16 is. As we were taken away, again, there was a bit of slapping around, kicking, even in the halls of this building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you afterwards detained in an isolation cell in this -- in the basement of this building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: Well, no. It's not a basement. It's a ground floor. I mean, the ground floor is on the ground. So people were taken out individually, brought back individually, interrogated, threatened, things like that, individually. Then perhaps only after midnight -- I don't even know what time it was. We were exhausted. We had suffered such a great deal. We somehow managed to calm down a bit in this one isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were all of you in one isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you beaten and questioned separately?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: Personally? From day one until the last day before I was exchanged, nobody ever interrogated me. Nobody told me why I was brought into custody, but nobody hit me, not even slightly, ever.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We are talking about this situation in the isolation cell. We are not talking about the other time.

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: Specifically, yes, yes, yes. Yes, I'm telling you quite specifically about this particular case. I was not interrogated.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the others, the other members of the work -- the metalwork shop, were they beaten on the ground floor in or in front of the isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: No, no, no. They were never beaten, really. This was just a tiny bit of beating, just a slap or two, a kick or two. But as for real big beatings, I think that they were administered individually. The people were taken out for beatings like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: On this occasion as well, in relation to the escape?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: I didn't really understand your question at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The question is: Was anybody severely beaten in relation to the escape of Mr. Zekovic? Not other occasions.

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: Well, I think that [redacted] was beaten. Then, I don't know, Mustafa Berber, people like that. I can't remember now. Spirjan, Sefik, also in the hall, he was punched in the stomach a few times.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know the person who's listed as number 73 on the sheet in front of you? Was he also involved in this?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: Yes, he was there too.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What happened to him, and why was he there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: I can't tell you for sure why he was brought into custody, but he was there with us. And apart from our isolation cell, all of us who were brought from the metalwork shop, others were brought to other isolation cells. We found out about that only after we got out, that they brought people from rooms to the other isolation cells.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What happened after Mr. Zekovic had been captured?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: Well, it was a bit hard to take psychologically and in terms of food and sleep. Everybody would come. Everybody would bring pressure to bear, thinking that somebody knew. And I don't know, I think it was the next day. I don't know what time it was. During the night, actually, Savo Todovic himself said, "I'm going to show you Ekrem Zekovic dead or alive. Not even a bird can leave Republika Srpska or come into it, let alone Ekrem Zekovic." And that's exactly the way it was. The next day they took room by room out, and that's how they took us out, too, and showed us Ekrem Zekovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the photo 7510. It's this, and it has to be on the ELMO. Not so close. A little bit wider. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you show us where Mr. Zekovic was when you saw him on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: The isolation cell is here. We were taken down. We lined up here. Practically all the guards were there. Among them was Ekrem Zekovic. This is the area there, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness was pointing at the area left from the tree which has the number "2" on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And where were you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: We were over there by that wall there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness is pointing at this wall on the left-hand side of the photo. Thank you, that's enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What did Mr. Zekovic look like when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: He was really depressed. His head was hanging down. Practically all the guards were there, and Savo himself walked up and said, "As I told, you, I'm going to show you Ekrem Zekovic dead or alive." And he pulled his head up and said, "See? He's all there, all in one piece." That was his comment, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was Mr. Krnojelac present on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I can't say for sure, although practically everyone was there, but I don't dare say whether Mr. Krnojelac was there or not. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: After, after Mr. Zekovic had been captured, how long did you continue to be in the isolation cell, you and the other members of the work group?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: After being taken back to the isolation cell, some kind of punishment followed. He lined us up in an isolation cell, and then he started meting out punishment. Somehow we were standing in a circle, and then he said 10 days, 15 days, 20 days in solitary confinement. I was back there, Sevko Kubat and I were, and I just thought if he goes on this way, more and more punishment, only God knows how many days I'm going to get. However, somehow the punishment started going down after a while, so I don't know what happened, but no punishment was meted out to me personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But how many days -- does it mean you could continue to the room immediately, or did you have to spend days in the isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: No, no. Isolation exclusively, and practically all of us from the metalwork shop were in one room. It's a small room. I don't know its exact dimensions, I just know it's pretty small, especially for such a number of people. And then we started getting less food. That's the way it was, day in, day out.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you said that he lined you up and he meted out punishment. Who is "he"?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: Yes, Savo Todovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And how many days did you spend in the isolation cell as a consequence of Mr. Zekovic's escape?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: I can't tell. I can't say exactly how many days. I know that a few persons allegedly went out for an exchange directly from that room, that so-called solitary confinement cell. And then after a certain number of days, five, six, seven days, I can't say exactly, they called me and Sevko Kubat to the workshop again because they needed a vehicle to leave once again. 16, 20, and it had to be prepared for the trip. And that is how the two of us got out of the solitary confinement cell on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Let us now talk about some exchanges. You had already mentioned in your previous statement here you have described how people disappeared in exchanges, and I don't want to discuss all these details again, just a few particular incidents. Were former workers from the Miljevina mine detained in the KP Dom? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: Former workers of the mine. There might have been some workers from the brown coal mine in Miljevina, too, but how many, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were any detainees taken out by Pero Elez at one point in time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: First of all, I think that was the first exchange. It was the first exchange, sort of. I can't remember the exact date. I keep going back to this. It's like a disease; dates, names, things like that. But I think that was the first exchange. I think he entered the compound at the very entrance gate, and he took some people away as if it were for the mine. I know three of them: Kemo Niksic, Dzemo Niksic, and Salko Sljivo. There were others as well. So I think that that was the first exchange, sort of. I mean, that they were taken out to work in the mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said you cannot give the exact date. Was it in the period while you were already working, or was it before that, that is, in the first 40, 50 days?

utterances.speaker: FWS-249
utterances.text: I think it was before I started going out to the metalwork shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And with the help of the usher, I would like you to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
